name: Light Pinkish Lilac
lede: Light Pinkish Lilac is a pale, pink-leaning step off [[lilac]], the purple named for the lilac blossom, filed twice over by Ridgway's 1912 atlas and the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955.

sections.title: A modifier on the lilac blossom
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light pinkish" over the parent [[lilac]], a word with a dark-blue ancestor that became the common-speech name for the first mass-market purple dye [1]. Ridgway's atlas plates it twice, at plate XXXVII and again at plate XLIV, both hue 65''-69''', tone f, and the ISCC-NBS system separately filed it in 1955 as block 249 [1]. Measured, it reads much lighter and far less saturated than lilac itself (lightness 83 against 71, chroma 10 against 25), near-white with only a faint pink-purple cast [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[pale-laelia-pink|Pale Laelia-Pink]], 3.2 units away and almost the same, with [[queen-pink|Queen Pink]] close behind, also 3.2 and purpler [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale lilac-pink in 37 of 23,781 paintings (0.16 percent, as photographed), rarer than 58 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It most often plays a light, in 73 percent of its strongest matches, and peaks in paintings from the 1900s at 1.9 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 1452, by Bartolomeo Caporali, 460 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
